notes:
User enjoys experimenting with cocktails, fresh garden herbs, gin styles, and practical flavor balancing. They favor Hendrick’s gin for its floral/cucumber notes and have made a Negroni about 10 times, refining it with friend Emma’s guidance; their established version uses Hendrick’s and Carpano Antica vermouth. They are curious about Campari alternatives and White Negronis, including dry vermouth and bitters such as Suze, Cynar, Aperol, Luxardo, and Meletti.

Current interests: making Lavender Gin Fizz and Grapefruit Basil Martini for a dinner party; lavender cocktails and basic syrup (1 cup sugar, 1 cup water, 1/4 cup dried buds; steep 10–15 minutes, strain, refrigerate up to two weeks), using lavender cautiously to avoid overpowering. They plan to infuse cucumber and mint into gin separately, then blend and taste over time, for possible Cucumber Gimlets. Lavender/grapefruit spirit infusions were also discussed.

They are exploring classic gin cocktails, especially Pimm’s Cup, Bee’s Knees (love gin+honey), and homemade 1:1 honey syrup warmed gently until dissolved, cooled and refrigerated up to two weeks. A Cranberry Sparkler was a dinner-party hit. Other gin cocktails suggested
trajectory: User enjoys experimenting with cocktails and fresh garden herbs, especially with Hendrick’s gin, whose floral/cucumber notes they favor. They have perfected/been refining a Negroni using Hendrick’s gin and Carpano Antica vermouth, made it about five times, and learned from Emma. They are curious about Campari alternatives and White Negronis, including dry vermouth and bitters such as Suze, Cynar, Aperol, Luxardo, and Meletti. They are interested in lavender cocktails and a basic lavender syrup (1 cup sugar, 1 cup water, 1/4 cup dried buds; steep 10–15 minutes, strain, refrigerate up to two weeks), with advice to use cautiously because lavender can overpower. They are exploring citrus pairings with gin and lavender; grapefruit and lemon are current interests, and recommendations included orange/blood orange, yuzu, kumquat, Satsuma, and bergamot. Overall, they seek practical recipe ideas, flavor-balancing tips, and inspiration for refreshing summer drinks.
